title: Preamble (প্রস্তাবনা)
content: We, the people of Bangladesh, having proclaimed our Independence on the 26th day of March, 1971 and through a historic war for national independence, established the independent, sovereign People's Republic of Bangladesh; Pledging that the high ideals of nationalism, socialism, democracy and secularism shall be the fundamental principles of the Constitution; Further pledging that it shall be a fundamental aim of the State to realise through the democratic process a socialist society, free from exploitation-a society in which the rule of law, fundamental human rights and freedom, equality and justice, political, economic and social, will be secured for all citizens...

articles.title: The Republic
articles.content: Bangladesh is a unitary, independent, sovereign Republic to be known as the People's Republic of Bangladesh.

articles.title: The State territory
articles.content: The territory of the Republic shall comprise the territories which immediately before the proclamation of independence constituted East Pakistan, and such other territories as may become included in Bangladesh.

articles.title: The State religion
articles.content: The state religion of the Republic is Islam, but the State shall ensure equal status and equal right in the practice of the Hindu, Buddhist, Christian and other religions.

articles.title: The State language
articles.content: The state language of the Republic is Bangla.

articles.title: National anthem, flag and emblem
articles.content: The national anthem is the first ten lines of 'Amar Sonar Bangla'. The national flag consists of a red circle on a green bottle field. The national emblem is the national flower Shapla (Nymphaea nouchali) resting on water, flanked by two sheaves of paddy, crested by three connected leaves of jute with two stars on each side.

articles.title: The Capital
articles.content: The capital of the Republic is Dhaka.

articles.title: Citizenship
articles.content: The citizenship of Bangladesh shall be determined and regulated by law. The people of Bangladesh shall be known as Bangalees as a nation and the citizens of Bangladesh shall be known as Bangladeshis.

articles.title: Supremacy of the Constitution
articles.content: All powers in the Republic belong to the people, and their exercise on behalf of the people shall be effected only under, and by the authority of, this Constitution. This Constitution is the supreme law of the Republic.

title: Fundamental Principles of State Policy (রাষ্ট্র পরিচালনার মূলনীতি)

articles.title: Fundamental principles
articles.content: The principles of nationalism, socialism, democracy and secularism shall constitute the fundamental principles of state policy.

articles.title: Nationalism
articles.content: The unity and solidarity of the Bangalee nation, which, deriving its identity from its language and culture, attained sovereign independence through a historic struggle, shall be the basis of Bangalee nationalism.

articles.title: Socialism and freedom from exploitation
articles.content: A socialist economic system shall be established with a view to ensuring the attainment of a just and egalitarian society.

articles.title: Democracy and human rights
articles.content: The Republic shall be a democracy in which fundamental human rights and freedoms and respect for the dignity and worth of the human person shall be guaranteed.

articles.title: Secularism and freedom of religion
articles.content: The principle of secularism shall be realised by the elimination of communalism, granting of political status in favour of any religion, and abuse of religion for political purposes.

articles.title: Provision of basic necessities
articles.content: It shall be a fundamental responsibility of the State to attain a steady improvement in the material and cultural standard of living of the people, by securing food, clothing, shelter, education and medical care.

articles.title: Free and compulsory education
articles.content: The State shall adopt effective measures for the purpose of establishing a uniform, mass-oriented and universal system of education and extending free and compulsory education to all children.

articles.title: Laws inconsistent with fundamental rights to be void
articles.content: All existing law inconsistent with the provisions of this Part shall, to the extent of such inconsistency, become void.

articles.title: Equality before law
articles.content: All citizens are equal before law and are entitled to equal protection of law.

articles.title: Discrimination on grounds of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth
articles.content: The State shall not discriminate against any citizen on grounds only of religion, race, caste, sex or place of birth. Women shall have equal rights with men in all spheres of the State and of public life.

articles.title: Right to protection of law
articles.content: To enjoy the protection of the law, and to be treated in accordance with law, and only in accordance with law, is the inalienable right of every citizen, and of every other person for the time being within Bangladesh.

articles.title: Protection of right to life and personal liberty
articles.content: No person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty save in accordance with law.

articles.title: Safeguards as to arrest and detention
articles.content: No person who is arrested shall be detained in custody without being informed, as soon as may be, of the grounds for such arrest, nor shall he be denied the right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of his choice. Every person arrested shall be produced before the nearest magistrate within twenty-four hours.

articles.title: Protection in respect of trial and punishment
articles.content: No person shall be convicted of any offence except for violation of a law in force at the time of the commission of the act charged. Every person accused of a criminal offence shall have the right to a speedy and public trial by an independent and impartial court or tribunal.

articles.title: Freedom of movement
articles.content: Subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by law, every citizen shall have the right to move freely throughout Bangladesh, to reside and settle in any place therein and to leave and re-enter Bangladesh.

articles.title: Freedom of assembly
articles.content: Every citizen shall have the right to assemble and to participate in public meetings and processions peacefully and without arms.

articles.title: Freedom of association
articles.content: Every citizen shall have the right to form associations or unions, subject to any reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the interests of morality or public order.

articles.title: Freedom of thought and conscience, and of speech
articles.content: Freedom of thought and conscience is guaranteed. The right of every citizen to freedom of speech and expression, and freedom of the press, are guaranteed subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by law.

articles.title: Freedom of profession or occupation
articles.content: Every citizen shall have the right to enter upon any lawful profession or occupation, and to conduct any lawful trade or business.

articles.title: Freedom of religion
articles.content: Every citizen has the right to profess, practise or propagate any religion. Every religious community or denomination has the right to establish, maintain and manage its religious institutions.

articles.title: Rights to property
articles.content: Every citizen shall have the right to acquire, hold, transfer or otherwise dispose of property, and no property shall be compulsorily acquired, nationalised or requisitioned save by authority of law.

articles.title: Enforcement of fundamental rights
articles.content: The right to move the High Court Division in accordance with clause (1) of article 102, for the enforcement of the rights conferred by this Part is guaranteed.

articles.title: The President
articles.content: There shall be a President of Bangladesh who shall be elected by members of Parliament in accordance with law. The President shall, as Head of State, take precedence over all other persons in the State.

articles.title: The Cabinet
articles.content: There shall be a Cabinet for Bangladesh having the Prime Minister at its head and comprising also such other Ministers as the Prime Minister may from time to time designate. The executive power of the Republic shall be exercised by or on the authority of the Prime Minister.

articles.title: The Attorney-General
articles.content: The President shall appoint a person who is qualified to be appointed as a Judge of the Supreme Court to be Attorney-General for Bangladesh. The Attorney-General shall perform such duties as may be assigned to him by the President.

articles.title: Establishment of Parliament
articles.content: There shall be a Parliament for Bangladesh (to be known as the House of the Nation and in Bangla as Jatiya Sangsad) in which the legislative powers of the Republic shall be vested. Parliament shall consist of three hundred members elected directly from single territorial constituencies, with fifty seats reserved exclusively for women.

articles.title: Qualifications and disqualifications for election to Parliament
articles.content: A person shall be qualified to be elected to, and to be a member of, Parliament if he is a citizen of Bangladesh and has attained the age of twenty-five years.

articles.title: Vacation of seat on resignation or voting against political party
articles.content: A person elected as a member of Parliament at an election in which he was nominated as a candidate by a political party shall vacate his seat if he resigns from that party or votes in Parliament against that party.

articles.title: Establishment of Supreme Court
articles.content: There shall be a Supreme Court for Bangladesh (to be known as the Supreme Court of Bangladesh) comprising the Appellate Division and the High Court Division. The Supreme Court shall consist of the Chief Justice and such number of other Judges as the President may deem it necessary to appoint.

articles.title: Jurisdiction of High Court Division
articles.content: The High Court Division shall have such original, appellate and other jurisdictions and powers as are conferred on it by this Constitution or any other law.

articles.title: Powers of High Court Division to issue certain orders and directions (Writ Jurisdiction)
articles.content: The High Court Division may, on the application of any person aggrieved, make an order directing a person performing functions in connection with the affairs of the Republic to refrain from doing that which he is not permitted by law to do (Prohibition), or to do that which he is required by law to do (Mandamus); declaring that any act done has been done without lawful authority (Certiorari); directing that a person in custody be brought before it so that it may satisfy itself that he is not being held without lawful authority (Habeas Corpus); and requiring a person holding a public office to show under what authority of law he claims to hold that office (Quo Warranto).

articles.title: Jurisdiction of Appellate Division
articles.content: The Appellate Division shall have jurisdiction to hear and determine appeals from judgments, decrees, orders or sentences of the High Court Division.

articles.title: Binding effect of Supreme Court judgments
articles.content: The law declared by the Appellate Division shall be binding on the High Court Division and the law declared by either division of the Supreme Court shall be binding on all courts subordinate thereto.

articles.title: Establishment of subordinate courts
articles.content: There shall be in addition to the Supreme Court such courts subordinate thereto as may be established by law.
